messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Lower serum vitamin D levels were associated with higher depression (HAMD) scores in acute stroke patients.
Sentence: "Lower vitamin D levels were associated with higher HAMD scores (P < 0.001)."
Measured as: HAMD scores
Population: 402 acute stroke patients
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (observational, measured)
Comparator: Higher vs lower vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 402
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: No association was found between baseline depressive symptom severity and baseline vitamin D concentration.
Sentence: "There was no association between the severity of depressive symptoms and the concentration of vitamin D at the beginning of the treatment."
Measured as: severity of depressive symptoms (GDS, HDRS)
Population: 140 patients of a psychogeriatric day-care unit
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level measured at start of treatment; patients below 30 µg/L received 1000 IU vitamin D daily
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 140
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale": "Both are observational cross-sectional or cohort associations at baseline, in different populations (acute stroke vs psychogeriatric day-care) with different depression scales (HAMD vs GDS/HDRS), so the disagreement reflects differing populations and measures rather than a clean design conflict.", "verdict": "genuine", "reason": "population", "also_differs": ["outcome_measure"], "detail": "population: acute stroke patients (n=402) vs psychogeriatric day-care patients (n=140); outcome: HAMD vs GDS/HDRS"}
